sentences.text: Suchodus was an extinct genus of marine crocodiliforms, a type of ancient reptile related to crocodiles, that possessed a streamlined body, powerful tail, and long jaws lined with sharp teeth.
This large marine predator fed on other large marine animals, indicating it hunted at the top of its local food chain.
Richard Lydekker first described the genus in 1890 based on a fragment of a lower jaw found near Peterborough.
Recent phylogenetic analyses have confirmed that Suchodus, meaning "crocodile tooth" in ancient Greek, is a valid genus of metriorhynchid.
The animal belongs to the metriorhynchid subfamily Geosaurinae and the tribe Geosaurini.
S. durobrivensis was originally the type species of Suchodus but was later considered a junior synonym of Metriorhynchus by Andrews in 1913.
Some authors include the species S. brachyrhynchus, originally described from the Callovian of Normandy, within the genus Suchodus.
Suchodus lived during the Middle to Late Jurassic periods in England and France.
The specific time range for the genus is the Callovian, spanning from 165.3 to 161.5 million years ago.
Andrews considered Suchodus a junior synonym of Metriorhynchus in 1913.
Studies from the 2000s questioned whether Suchodus is a synonym of Metriorhynchus.
The placement of S. brachyrhynchus in Suchodus is debated, with some assigning it to Metriorhynchus or a new genus.
